questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement, whose negotiations were concluded on 27 January 2026:
1. The EU becomes India's 22nd FTA partner.
2. Negotiations began in 2007, were suspended in 2013 and were relaunched in 2022.
3. The EU granted tariff concessions on sugar, ethanol and rice.
4. The deal is to take effect without the need for ratification by EU Member States.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The announcement at the 16th India-EU Summit made the EU India's 22nd FTA partner, after talks that began in 2007, stalled in 2013 and restarted in 2022. The EU gave no concessions on sensitive farm goods such as sugar, ethanol, rice, soft wheat, beef, poultry, milk powders, bananas and honey. The text still needs legal scrubbing and approval by the European Council and consent of the European Parliament, so only statements 1 and 2 hold.
questions.s: European Commission IP Helpdesk, Jan 2026; Vision IAS

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's visit to India on 12-13 January 2026:
1. It was his first visit to India as Chancellor.
2. It marked 25 years of the India-Germany strategic partnership and 75 years of diplomatic relations.
3. Germany announced its intent to join the Quad.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Merz held talks with Prime Minister Modi at Mahatma Mandir, Gandhinagar, and attended the International Kite Festival in Ahmedabad. Germany announced intent to join MILAN, the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium and Tarang Shakti, and backed the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC); it did not announce an intent to join the Quad.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the visit of UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan to New Delhi on 19 January 2026:
1. India and the UAE signed a Letter of Intent toward a Strategic Defence Partnership.
2. The 10-year LNG supply deal starting in 2028 is between IOC and ADNOC Gas.
3. The leaders set a target of doubling bilateral trade from USD 100 billion to USD 200 billion by 2032.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The LNG deal is between HPCL and ADNOC Gas (0.5 million tonnes a year), not IOC. The Letter of Intent on a Strategic Defence Partnership and the USD 200 billion trade target by 2032, building on the 2022 CEPA, are correct. The leaders also agreed to explore Small Modular Reactors after India's SHANTI Act, 2025, and a 'House of India' in Abu Dhabi.
questions.s: UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 19 Jan 2026

questions.q:
With the conclusion of the India-New Zealand FTA talks in December 2025, India has trade agreements with every RCEP member except China. Consider the following statements about India's recent trade agreements:
1. The India-Oman CEPA was signed in December 2025.
2. The India-UK CETA was signed in July 2025.
3. The India-Australia ECTA came into effect in December 2022.
4. The India-EFTA TEPA was signed in 2022.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Oman CEPA (December 2025), the UK CETA (July 2025) and the Australia ECTA (in effect December 2022) are correctly dated. The India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement was signed in March 2024, not 2022. The UAE CEPA came into force in 2022.

questions.q: Which one of the following is correct about the Wangchhu Hydroelectric Project in Bhutan on which Adani Group began construction in January 2026?
o: A 570 MW run-of-river project in Chukha district in which Adani Power holds 49 per cent and Druk Green Power Corporation 51 per cent
A 570 MW run-of-river project in which Adani Power holds 51 per cent and Druk Green Power Corporation 49 per cent
A 570 MW storage project with a large reservoir in Chukha district
A 1,720 MW run-of-river project in Chukha district built by NHPC
questions.e: The project is a run-of-river scheme on the Wangchu (Raidak) river, developed on a build-own-operate-transfer basis by a joint venture in which Bhutan's Druk Green Power holds the majority 51 per cent. Winter power meets Bhutan's own demand and summer surplus is exported to India.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Shaksgam Valley, in the news in January 2026:
1. It lies north of the Siachen Glacier.
2. It was ceded by Pakistan to China under the 1963 Sino-Pakistan Boundary Agreement, which India does not recognise.
3. It is another name for Aksai Chin.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India rejected China's CPEC-linked infrastructure activity in the Trans-Karakoram Tract (Shaksgam Valley) as illegal and invalid and reaffirmed that it is an integral part of India. The valley, ceded by Pakistan in 1963, lies north of Siachen; Aksai Chin is a different region in eastern Ladakh.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about BRICS in 2026:
1. India holds the BRICS chairship for 2026 and is hosting the summit in New Delhi.
2. The RBI recommended putting the linking of BRICS central bank digital currencies on the summit agenda.
3. The 2025 BRICS declaration on payment-system interoperability was adopted at Johannesburg.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: BRICS chairship rotates annually, and India's 2026 chair was backed by the UAE in the India-UAE joint statement of 19 January 2026. The RBI's CBDC-linking proposal builds on the 2025 declaration in Rio de Janeiro, not Johannesburg.

questions.q: Spain joined the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI), launched by India in November 2019. Which one of the following IPOI pillars is correctly matched with its lead partner countries?
o: Maritime security: Japan and the US
Trade and connectivity: France and Indonesia
Science and technology: the UK and India
questions.e: IPOI has seven pillars: maritime security (UK, India), maritime ecology (Australia, Thailand), maritime resources (France, Indonesia), capacity building (Germany), disaster risk reduction (India, Bangladesh), science and technology (Italy, Singapore), and trade and connectivity (Japan, US). Only the maritime ecology pairing is correct.
questions.h: Seven pillars: UK-India secure the seas

questions.q: India became a signatory to the Pax Silica Declaration in January 2026. Pax Silica is best described as
o: a United States-led initiative to build secure, resilient technology supply chains spanning semiconductors, AI infrastructure and critical minerals
a WTO plurilateral agreement on tariffs for digital trade
an India-led grouping of Indo-Pacific navies for maritime domain awareness
a UN framework on the safe use of artificial intelligence
questions.e: Pax Silica aims to cut coercive dependencies and protect sensitive technology across the semiconductor, AI, critical-minerals, advanced-manufacturing and compute chain; Japan, South Korea, Singapore, the UK and Israel are among the members. India also signed a joint statement on an India-US AI Opportunity Partnership as a bilateral addendum.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Weimar Triangle, in which India's External Affairs Minister took part for the first time in January 2026:
1. It was formed in 1991 to anchor German-Polish reconciliation.
2. It has no institutional structure.
3. India joined it as a full member in January 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Weimar Triangle of France, Germany and Poland was created on 29 August 1991 by a joint declaration of foreign ministers in Weimar, and it has no secretariat or formal structure. India's participation was an engagement, not membership.

questions.q:
The 2nd India-Arab Foreign Ministers' Meeting was scheduled for New Delhi on 30-31 January 2026. Consider the following statements about the League of Arab States:
1. It was founded in Cairo in 1945 and is headquartered there.
2. It has 22 member states.
3. Decisions of its Council are binding on all members irrespective of how they voted.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Arab League was set up in Cairo in March 1945 and has 22 members; its Council gives one vote to each member and decisions bind only those that voted for them. Syria returned in May 2023 after a 12-year suspension. India's formal engagement dates from a March 2002 MoU, followed by the Arab-India Cooperation Forum in 2008.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the events in Venezuela in January 2026:
1. On 3 January 2026 United States forces struck Caracas and captured President Nicolas Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores.
2. The operation was named Operation Absolute Resolve.
3. The UN Security Council held an emergency meeting on 5 January.
4. Maduro was flown to Miami to face narco-terrorism charges.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The strikes of 3 January 2026, codenamed Operation Absolute Resolve, ended with Maduro and Cilia Flores being flown to New York, not Miami, to face narco-terrorism charges; the Security Council met in emergency session on 5 January. Venezuela's Supreme Court ordered Vice President Delcy Rodriguez to serve as interim president. Three statements are correct.

questions.q: The United States announced in January 2026 its withdrawal from 66 international organisations, including the International Solar Alliance (ISA). Which one of the following is correct about the ISA?
o: It was launched by India and France at COP21 in Paris in 2015 and is headquartered in Gurugram
It was launched by India and the US at COP26 in Glasgow in 2021 and is headquartered in Gurugram
It was launched by India and France at COP21 in Paris in 2015 and is headquartered in Paris
It was launched by India and Germany at COP28 in 2023 and is headquartered in New Delhi
questions.e: The ISA was launched by India and France at COP21 in Paris in 2015 and is headquartered in Gurugram, Haryana; the US had joined in 2021. The presidential memorandum of around 7 January 2026 covered 66 organisations, including 31 UN entities such as the IPCC and UN DESA.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'Board of Peace' launched at the World Economic Forum in Davos in January 2026:
1. It was launched on 22 January 2026 by US President Donald Trump.
2. India attended the launch and signed its charter.
3. It was set up for Gaza under UN Security Council Resolution 2803 (2025), with a mandate to 31 December 2027.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Trump launched the Board of Peace on 22 January 2026, and it was set up under UNSC Resolution 2803 (2025) with a mandate to 31 December 2027. India was invited but neither accepted nor declined and did not attend the launch, while Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif did. Two statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Greenland episode at the World Economic Forum in Davos on 21 January 2026:
1. US President Trump dropped a threatened tariff on eight European countries.
2. He said the US would not use force to acquire Greenland.
3. China's 'Polar Silk Road' was announced jointly with Canada in 2017.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Trump announced a 'framework of a future deal' on Greenland, dropped the tariff threat on eight European countries and ruled out force. The Polar Silk Road was announced jointly by China and Russia in 2017, and US remarks on Greenland revived debate on it, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q: Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 January 2026. It thus became the ___ member of the eurozone.
questions.e: Bulgaria replaced the lev and became the 21st eurozone member. Croatia, which joined in 2023, was the 20th. The euro was launched on 1 January 1999 with 11 countries; Sweden, Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Romania and Denmark remain outside.

questions.q: Which one of the following sets of countries began two-year terms as non-permanent members of the UN Security Council on 1 January 2026?
o: Pakistan, Colombia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Latvia and Liberia
Bahrain, Colombia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Latvia and Liberia
Bahrain, Colombia, Greece, Latvia and Liberia
Bahrain, Colombia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Latvia and Somalia
questions.e: The General Assembly elected these five in June 2025; their terms run through 2027. The Council has five permanent and ten non-permanent members, and non-permanent seats are filled for two-year terms, with five replaced each year.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Agreement on Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ), or the High Seas Treaty:
1. It entered into force on 17 January 2026.
2. It was adopted in 2023 under the Convention on Biological Diversity.
3. India signed the agreement in 2024, but its ratification was pending.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The treaty entered into force 120 days after the 60th ratification. It was adopted under UNCLOS (1982), not the CBD. Its four pillars are marine genetic resources and benefit sharing, area-based management tools such as marine protected areas, environmental impact assessments, and capacity building and technology transfer.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Chagos archipelago, in the news in January 2026:
1. The United Kingdom cancelled its agreement to transfer the archipelago to Mauritius after criticism from US President Trump.
2. The agreement lets the UK retain a 99-year lease on the Diego Garcia base.
3. The International Court of Justice's 2019 advisory opinion found the UK's 1965 detachment of Chagos from Mauritius unlawful.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The UK defended, not cancelled, its agreement to transfer sovereignty to Mauritius while keeping a 99-year lease on Diego Garcia. The deal rests partly on the ICJ's 2019 advisory opinion that the 1965 detachment was unlawful.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Akash-NG (New Generation) surface-to-air missile, whose user evaluation trials DRDO completed in January 2026:
1. The Indian Army was the user for the trials.
2. It has a range of up to 70 km, against about 30 km for the original Akash.
3. It uses a solid rocket motor instead of a ramjet and has about 96 per cent indigenous content.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Indian Air Force, not the Army, was the user for the Akash-NG trials. The missile reaches up to 70 km at Mach 2.5 with a solid rocket motor in place of the original's ramjet, and Bharat Dynamics and Bharat Electronics are the production partners.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 78th Army Day, observed on 15 January 2026:
1. The parade was held in Jaipur, the first Army Day parade held outside a cantonment.
2. Army Day marks the day in 1949 when Field Marshal K.M. Cariappa became the first Indian Commander-in-Chief.
3. Each new Bhairav Battalion has about 1,000 personnel.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Jaipur hosted the first Army Day parade outside a cantonment, where the new Bhairav Battalions made their debut and the Army named 2026 the 'Year of Networking and Data Centricity'. Each Bhairav battalion is small, with about 200 to 250 personnel from infantry, artillery, air defence and signals, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Long Range Anti-Ship Hypersonic Missile (LR-AShM), showcased at the 77th Republic Day parade on 26 January 2026:
1. It was showcased for the first time at the parade.
2. It is a hypersonic cruise missile powered by a scramjet engine.
3. It has a range of about 1,500 km and can reach up to Mach 10.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The DRDO missile was displayed for the first time and has a range of about 1,500 km at up to Mach 10. It is a hypersonic glide missile using a two-stage solid rocket motor, not a scramjet-powered cruise missile; scramjets belong to the separate Hypersonic Cruise Missile programme. A successful test was held in November 2024 and induction is expected in 2 to 3 years.
questions.s: Vajiram & Ravi Prelims pointers, 9 Jan 2026; Vision IAS

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about indigenous defence systems in the news in January 2026:
1. Pralay is a short-range surface-to-surface quasi-ballistic missile developed by DRDO with a range of 150 to 500 km.
2. Suryastra is a universal multi-calibre rocket launcher for which the Army signed a Rs 293 crore contract with a private firm, with a strike range of up to 300 km.
3. The MPATGM is a vehicle-mounted, wire-guided second-generation anti-tank missile.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: DRDO fired two Pralay missiles from the Odisha coast, and the Army contracted NIBE Limited, working with Israel, for Suryastra. The Man Portable Anti-Tank Guided Missile is a third-generation, shoulder-launched weapon with an imaging infrared seeker, tested against a moving target, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
Statement-I: In January 2026, NATGRID was integrated with the National Population Register, giving authorised agencies access to family-level data of about 119 crore residents.
Statement-II: NATGRID was conceived in 2009 after the 26/11 attacks.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct, but the 2009 origin of NATGRID after the 26/11 attacks does not explain why it was linked to the NPR in 2026. NATGRID became operational in 2023 and access has been extended to State police officers of SP rank; the NPR was last updated in 2015.

questions.q: INSV Kaundinya, which reached Muscat in Oman from Porbandar in January 2026, is notable as
o: India's first stitched ship, built using the ancient Tankai method
the sail training ship on the 10-month Lokayan 26 expedition
the first indigenous pollution control vessel of the Indian Coast Guard
a DRDO ship used for the Sagar Maitri oceanographic mission
questions.e: INSV Kaundinya is a stitched ship, with planks sewn together rather than nailed, made by the ancient Tankai method; it sailed on its maiden voyage from Porbandar to Muscat's Port Sultan Qaboos. Lokayan 26 is the INS Sudarshini expedition, ICGS Samudra Pratap is the pollution control vessel, and Sagar Maitri uses INS Sagardhwani.
